q24456.en: It is forbidden to use a car on public roads when the vehicle is not covered by third-party liability insurance.

explain.short: Third-party insurance (RCA) is compulsory. Without it the car may not be used on public roads, even if parked.
explain.rule: To drive on public roads you need: the right licence, a registered vehicle with plates, valid third-party insurance (RCA). You do NOT need to carry the tax receipt or the ownership certificate, and the car may belong to someone else.
explain.trap: 'responsabilità civile' is the compulsory insurance (RCA) that pays for damage you cause to others.

sceneParams.caption: No RCA insurance = no driving

q24457.en: It is forbidden to drive a car on public roads when you do not hold the driving licence needed for that type of vehicle.

explain.short: Each vehicle type needs its licence category. Driving without the right one is forbidden.
explain.rule: To drive on public roads you need: the right licence, a registered vehicle with plates, valid third-party insurance (RCA). You do NOT need to carry the tax receipt or the ownership certificate, and the car may belong to someone else.
explain.trap: 'necessaria per quel tipo di veicolo': not any licence, the right category for that vehicle.

sceneParams.caption: You need the right licence category

q24458.en: As a rule, it is forbidden to drive on public roads a car that is not registered.

explain.short: A car must be registered (immatricolato) and have plates to use public roads. There are a few exceptions, like trial plates, so 'as a rule'.
explain.rule: To drive on public roads you need: the right licence, a registered vehicle with plates, valid third-party insurance (RCA). You do NOT need to carry the tax receipt or the ownership certificate, and the car may belong to someone else.
explain.trap: 'di norma' (as a rule) makes it right: there are exceptions such as the trial plate (targa prova).

sceneParams.caption: Not registered: as a rule forbidden
lines: Car must be registered, with plates
Not registered: as a rule forbidden

q24459.en: It is forbidden to use a car on public roads when you do not have with you the receipt of payment of the ownership tax.

explain.short: You must pay the car tax (bollo), but you do not have to carry the receipt. The payment is checked in the records.
explain.rule: To drive on public roads you need: the right licence, a registered vehicle with plates, valid third-party insurance (RCA). You do NOT need to carry the tax receipt or the ownership certificate, and the car may belong to someone else.
explain.trap: 'con sé' (with you) is the trap: paying is required, carrying the receipt is not.

sceneParams.caption: Tax receipt does not have to be carried
lines: Receipt: no need to carry it

q24460.en: It is forbidden to drive on public roads with a car fitted with a trial plate.

explain.short: The trial plate (targa prova) is made exactly for using unregistered vehicles on the road for tests and transfers. So it is allowed.
explain.rule: To drive on public roads you need: the right licence, a registered vehicle with plates, valid third-party insurance (RCA). You do NOT need to carry the tax receipt or the ownership certificate, and the car may belong to someone else.
explain.trap: 'targa prova' (trial plate) is legal: it is the exception to the registration rule.

sceneParams.caption: Trial plate: driving is allowed

q24461.en: It is forbidden to use a car on public roads when the registration document is in the name of a person other than the driver.

explain.short: You may drive a car that belongs to someone else, for example a friend's or a family car. The owner does not have to be the driver.
explain.rule: To drive on public roads you need: the right licence, a registered vehicle with plates, valid third-party insurance (RCA). You do NOT need to carry the tax receipt or the ownership certificate, and the car may belong to someone else.
explain.trap: 'intestata a persona diversa' (in another person's name) is normal and allowed.

sceneParams.caption: You may drive a car owned by someone else
lines: You may drive it with your licence

keywords.en: a person other than the driver

q24462.en: On public roads it is forbidden to use a car if its warranty has expired.

explain.short: The warranty (garanzia) is a deal between buyer and seller for repairs. It has nothing to do with the right to drive.
explain.rule: To drive on public roads you need: the right licence, a registered vehicle with plates, valid third-party insurance (RCA). You do NOT need to carry the tax receipt or the ownership certificate, and the car may belong to someone else.
explain.trap: 'garanzia' is the shop warranty, not the insurance: when it expires you can still drive.

sceneParams.caption: Expired warranty does not stop you

q24463.en: It is forbidden to use a car on public roads when you do not have the certificate of ownership with you.

explain.short: The certificate of ownership is not a document you must carry while driving. You carry the licence, the registration document and the insurance.
explain.rule: To drive on public roads you need: the right licence, a registered vehicle with plates, valid third-party insurance (RCA). You do NOT need to carry the tax receipt or the ownership certificate, and the car may belong to someone else.
explain.trap: 'certificato di proprietà' is not in the list of documents to carry: do not mix it up with the 'carta di circolazione'.

sceneParams.caption: Ownership certificate: no need to carry it

q24464.en: To be allowed on the road, a car must have identification plates, so that the owner of the vehicle can be traced.

explain.short: Plates identify the vehicle, so police can find who it belongs to. Without plates the car cannot circulate.
explain.rule: A car on the road must have its plates, its registration document (carta di circolazione) and the warning triangle. The only compulsory insurance is third-party (RCA), not 'kasko'.
explain.trap: 'affinché sia possibile risalire all'intestatario' explains why: the plate leads to the owner.

sceneParams.caption: Plates show who owns the car

q24465.en: To be allowed on the road, a car must have its registration document.

explain.short: The registration document (carta di circolazione) shows the car's data and must be kept on board, ready to show the police.
explain.rule: A car on the road must have its plates, its registration document (carta di circolazione) and the warning triangle. The only compulsory insurance is third-party (RCA), not 'kasko'.
explain.trap: 'carta di circolazione' (registration document) is one of the documents always kept in the car.

sceneParams.caption: Registration document on board
lines: Show it to the police on request

q24467.en: To be allowed on the road, a car must have the portable warning sign (triangle).

explain.short: Every car must carry the warning triangle, to signal the car when it stops in a dangerous place.
explain.rule: A car on the road must have its plates, its registration document (carta di circolazione) and the warning triangle. The only compulsory insurance is third-party (RCA), not 'kasko'.
explain.trap: 'segnale mobile di pericolo' is just the official name of the triangle.

sceneParams.caption: Warning triangle: compulsory
lines: Use it when you stop on the road

q24468.en: To be allowed on the road, a car must have a 'kasko' type insurance policy.

explain.short: Only third-party insurance (RCA) is compulsory. 'Kasko' covers damage to your own car and is optional.
explain.rule: A car on the road must have its plates, its registration document (carta di circolazione) and the warning triangle. The only compulsory insurance is third-party (RCA), not 'kasko'.
explain.trap: 'kasko' is extra insurance for your own car: it is a free choice.

sceneParams.caption: Kasko is optional; RCA is compulsory

q24469.en: Vehicle plates must be fixed firmly and in the correct position.

explain.short: A plate must not fall off or be in the wrong place: it must be easy to see and read.
explain.rule: Plates must be fixed firmly in the right place, always readable, clean and never altered or bent. Cars for driving lessons carry 'P' panels front and back.
explain.trap: 'saldamente' (firmly) and 'posizione corretta': both are required.

sceneParams.caption: Plates: firm and in the right place

q24470.en: Vehicle plates must always be clearly readable.

explain.short: Police and cameras must read the plate at any time. So it must always be readable.
explain.rule: Plates must be fixed firmly in the right place, always readable, clean and never altered or bent. Cars for driving lessons carry 'P' panels front and back.
explain.trap: 'sempre' (always) is right here: a plate must be readable at all times.

sceneParams.caption: Plates always readable
lines: Police must read it at any time

q24471.en: Vehicle plates must not be dirty.

explain.short: A dirty plate cannot be read well. Keep it clean, for example after mud or snow.
explain.rule: Plates must be fixed firmly in the right place, always readable, clean and never altered or bent. Cars for driving lessons carry 'P' panels front and back.
explain.trap: 'sporche' (dirty): a dirty plate is not readable, so it is not allowed.

sceneParams.caption: Keep plates clean

q24472.en: Vehicle plates must not be tampered with or forged.

explain.short: Changing or faking a plate hides who owns the car. It is a serious offence.
explain.rule: Plates must be fixed firmly in the right place, always readable, clean and never altered or bent. Cars for driving lessons carry 'P' panels front and back.
explain.trap: 'manomesse' (tampered) and 'contraffatte' (forged): both are forbidden.

sceneParams.caption: Never alter or fake a plate

q24473.en: Cars used for driving practice must have, both at the front and at the rear, special retroreflective panels with the letter 'P' (learner).

explain.short: A learner car must show the 'P' panel front and back, so other drivers know a beginner is driving.
explain.rule: Plates must be fixed firmly in the right place, always readable, clean and never altered or bent. Cars for driving lessons carry 'P' panels front and back.
explain.trap: 'sia anteriormente che posteriormente' (both front and rear): one panel only is not enough.

sceneParams.caption: Learner car: 'P' panel front and rear

q24474.en: Vehicle plates may be bent to fit their holder better.

explain.short: A bent plate is altered and can be hard to read. Plates must stay as they are.
explain.rule: Plates must be fixed firmly in the right place, always readable, clean and never altered or bent. Cars for driving lessons carry 'P' panels front and back.
explain.trap: 'piegate' (bent) makes it wrong: you may not change the shape of a plate.

sceneParams.caption: Never bend a plate
lines: Plate must stay flat and readable

q24475.en: With an AM licence you may drive light quadricycles.

explain.short: The AM licence covers mopeds and light quadricycles (small, slow four-wheel vehicles, 'minicar').
explain.rule: AM licence: from 14 years, with theory and driving exams. It covers mopeds with 2 or 3 wheels and light quadricycles. It does not cover motorbikes or non-light quadricycles.
explain.trap: 'leggeri' (light) is the key: light quadricycles yes, non-light ones no.

sceneParams.caption: AM: light quadricycles allowed

q24476.en: With an AM licence you may drive two-wheel mopeds.

explain.short: Two-wheel mopeds (ciclomotori, scooters) are the main AM vehicles.
explain.rule: AM licence: from 14 years, with theory and driving exams. It covers mopeds with 2 or 3 wheels and light quadricycles. It does not cover motorbikes or non-light quadricycles.
explain.trap: 'ciclomotori' are mopeds, not motorbikes (motocicli).

sceneParams.caption: AM: two-wheel mopeds allowed

q24477.en: With an AM licence you may drive three-wheel mopeds.

explain.short: AM covers all mopeds, with two or three wheels.
explain.rule: AM licence: from 14 years, with theory and driving exams. It covers mopeds with 2 or 3 wheels and light quadricycles. It does not cover motorbikes or non-light quadricycles.
explain.trap: 'tre ruote' (three wheels) is still a moped: AM is enough.

sceneParams.caption: AM: three-wheel mopeds allowed

q24478.en: You can get the AM licence at 14 years of age.

explain.short: The minimum age for the AM licence in Italy is 14.
explain.rule: AM licence: from 14 years, with theory and driving exams. It covers mopeds with 2 or 3 wheels and light quadricycles. It does not cover motorbikes or non-light quadricycles.
explain.trap: The number 14 is correct for AM.

sceneParams.caption: AM licence: from 14 years

q24479.en: The AM licence allows you to drive mopeds with a thermal engine of not more than 50 cm3.

explain.short: A moped with a fuel (thermal) engine has at most 50 cm3. That is exactly an AM vehicle.
explain.rule: AM licence: from 14 years, with theory and driving exams. It covers mopeds with 2 or 3 wheels and light quadricycles. It does not cover motorbikes or non-light quadricycles.
explain.trap: 'non superiore a 50 cm3' (not more than 50 cm3) is the moped limit, so it is correct.

sceneParams.caption: AM: mopeds up to 50 cm3

q24481.en: With an AM licence you may drive two-wheel mopeds, while to drive three-wheel mopeds you need an A1 licence.

explain.short: AM covers mopeds with two AND three wheels. You do not need A1 for a three-wheel moped.
explain.rule: AM licence: from 14 years, with theory and driving exams. It covers mopeds with 2 or 3 wheels and light quadricycles. It does not cover motorbikes or non-light quadricycles.
explain.trap: 'occorre la patente A1' (you need A1) is wrong: AM is enough.

sceneParams.caption: Three-wheel mopeds: AM is enough

q24482.en: The AM licence allows anyone aged 14 to drive mopeds in all European Union countries.

explain.short: At 14 the AM licence is valid in Italy. Other EU countries may set a higher minimum age, so it is not valid everywhere at 14.
explain.rule: AM licence: from 14 years, with theory and driving exams. It covers mopeds with 2 or 3 wheels and light quadricycles. It does not cover motorbikes or non-light quadricycles.
explain.trap: 'in tutti i paesi dell'Unione Europea' (in all EU countries) is the trap: at 14 it is only valid in Italy.

sceneParams.caption: At 14, AM is valid in Italy, not all the EU

q24482.reviewNote: Explanation says other EU countries may require a higher age; no number given on purpose.

q24483.en: With an AM licence you may drive non-light quadricycles with power up to 7 kW.

explain.short: AM covers only LIGHT quadricycles. Non-light quadricycles need the B1 (or B) licence.
explain.rule: AM licence: from 14 years, with theory and driving exams. It covers mopeds with 2 or 3 wheels and light quadricycles. It does not cover motorbikes or non-light quadricycles.
explain.trap: 'non leggeri' (non-light) is the trap: AM stops at light quadricycles.

sceneParams.caption: Non-light quadricycles: not with AM

q24484.en: The AM licence allows you to drive motorbikes, as long as they have an electric engine.

explain.short: AM covers mopeds, not motorbikes (motocicli). An electric engine does not change the category.
explain.rule: AM licence: from 14 years, with theory and driving exams. It covers mopeds with 2 or 3 wheels and light quadricycles. It does not cover motorbikes or non-light quadricycles.
explain.trap: 'motocicli' (motorbikes) are not mopeds; 'elettrico' does not make them AM vehicles.

sceneParams.caption: Motorbikes need A1, A2 or A, even electric
lines: Not with AM: A1, A2 or A

q24485.en: The AM licence can be issued without taking the theory and practical exams, as long as the applicant is of age.

explain.short: Everyone must pass the theory and driving exams for the AM licence. Being an adult gives no exemption.
explain.rule: AM licence: from 14 years, with theory and driving exams. It covers mopeds with 2 or 3 wheels and light quadricycles. It does not cover motorbikes or non-light quadricycles.
explain.trap: 'senza dover sostenere gli esami' (without exams) is wrong: exams are always needed.

sceneParams.caption: AM always needs theory and driving exams

q24486.en: The AM licence held for at least 3 years allows you to drive motorbikes with power up to 11 kW.

explain.short: AM never grows into a motorbike licence with time. For 11 kW motorbikes you need the A1 licence.
explain.rule: AM licence: from 14 years, with theory and driving exams. It covers mopeds with 2 or 3 wheels and light quadricycles. It does not cover motorbikes or non-light quadricycles.
explain.trap: 'da almeno 3 anni' (for at least 3 years) is invented: time does not upgrade AM.

sceneParams.caption: AM never becomes a motorbike licence

q24488.en: With an A1 licence you may drive motorbikes (with or without sidecar) up to 125 cm3, power not over 11 kW and power/weight ratio not over 0.1 kW/kg.

explain.short: These are exactly the three limits of an A1 motorbike: 125 cm3, 11 kW and 0.1 kW/kg.
explain.rule: A1 licence: from 16 years. Motorbikes up to 125 cm3, 11 kW and 0.1 kW/kg; tricycles up to 15 kW; small farm machines; and all AM vehicles. It never turns into A2 or A by itself.
explain.trap: All three limits must be met together: size, power and power/weight.

q24489.en: With an A1 licence you may drive motor tricycles with power not over 15 kW.

explain.short: A1 covers tricycles up to 15 kW. More powerful tricycles need the A licence.
explain.rule: A1 licence: from 16 years. Motorbikes up to 125 cm3, 11 kW and 0.1 kW/kg; tricycles up to 15 kW; small farm machines; and all AM vehicles. It never turns into A2 or A by itself.
explain.trap: 'non superiore a 15 kW' (not over 15 kW) is the correct A1 limit.

sceneParams.caption: A1: tricycles up to 15 kW

q24490.en: With an A1 licence you may drive farm machines that stay within the size and mass limits set for motor vehicles of the motorbike class (motoveicoli).

explain.short: Small farm machines, within the size and weight of motoveicoli, can be driven with A1.
explain.rule: A1 licence: from 16 years. Motorbikes up to 125 cm3, 11 kW and 0.1 kW/kg; tricycles up to 15 kW; small farm machines; and all AM vehicles. It never turns into A2 or A by itself.
explain.trap: 'nei limiti di sagoma e di massa' (within size and mass limits) is the condition that makes it true.

sceneParams.caption: A1: small farm machines allowed

keywords.it: limiti di sagoma e di massa

q24491.en: The A1 licence can be obtained by anyone who is at least 16 years old.

explain.short: The minimum age for A1 is 16.
explain.rule: A1 licence: from 16 years. Motorbikes up to 125 cm3, 11 kW and 0.1 kW/kg; tricycles up to 15 kW; small farm machines; and all AM vehicles. It never turns into A2 or A by itself.
explain.trap: 16 is the correct number for A1 (AM is 14, A2 is 18).

sceneParams.caption: A1: from 16 years

q24493.en: The A1 licence also allows you to drive the vehicles that can be driven with the AM licence.

explain.short: Each motorbike licence includes the lower ones. A1 includes AM: mopeds and light quadricycles.
explain.rule: A1 licence: from 16 years. Motorbikes up to 125 cm3, 11 kW and 0.1 kW/kg; tricycles up to 15 kW; small farm machines; and all AM vehicles. It never turns into A2 or A by itself.
explain.trap: 'anche' (also): A1 covers its own vehicles plus all AM vehicles.

sceneParams.caption: A1 includes AM vehicles

q24494.en: The A1 licence can be obtained only by someone who already holds the AM licence.

explain.short: You can take A1 directly at 16. You do not need AM first.
explain.rule: A1 licence: from 16 years. Motorbikes up to 125 cm3, 11 kW and 0.1 kW/kg; tricycles up to 15 kW; small farm machines; and all AM vehicles. It never turns into A2 or A by itself.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) makes it wrong: AM is not a required first step.

sceneParams.caption: A1 does not require AM first

q24495.en: The A1 licence allows you to drive all motorbikes up to 125 cm3.

explain.short: Engine size is not the only limit: an A1 motorbike also needs at most 11 kW and 0.1 kW/kg. A powerful 125 is not allowed.
explain.rule: A1 licence: from 16 years. Motorbikes up to 125 cm3, 11 kW and 0.1 kW/kg; tricycles up to 15 kW; small farm machines; and all AM vehicles. It never turns into A2 or A by itself.
explain.trap: 'tutti' (all) is the trap: some 125 cm3 motorbikes are too powerful for A1.

sceneParams.caption: Not all 125s: also 11 kW and 0.1 kW/kg

q24496.en: With an A1 licence you may drive tricycles with power over 15 kW, but only if the driver is of age.

explain.short: Tricycles over 15 kW need the A licence (and age 21). A1 stops at 15 kW at any age.
explain.rule: A1 licence: from 16 years. Motorbikes up to 125 cm3, 11 kW and 0.1 kW/kg; tricycles up to 15 kW; small farm machines; and all AM vehicles. It never turns into A2 or A by itself.
explain.trap: 'superiore a 15 kW' (over 15 kW): age does not change the A1 limit.

sceneParams.caption: Tricycle over 15 kW: A licence, not A1
lines: Not with A1, at any age

q24497.en: With an A1 licence you may drive non-exceptional work machines.

explain.short: Work machines (macchine operatrici, like road-works vehicles) are not A1 vehicles; they need the B licence.
explain.rule: A1 licence: from 16 years. Motorbikes up to 125 cm3, 11 kW and 0.1 kW/kg; tricycles up to 15 kW; small farm machines; and all AM vehicles. It never turns into A2 or A by itself.
explain.trap: 'macchine operatrici' (work machines) are not 'macchine agricole' (farm machines): only small farm machines go with A1.

sceneParams.caption: Work machines: not with A1

q24498.en: The A1 licence lets a driver under 18 carry a passenger, but only if the passenger is of age.

explain.short: Whether you may carry a passenger depends on the vehicle: the registration document must allow a passenger seat. The passenger's age is not the rule.
explain.rule: A1 licence: from 16 years. Motorbikes up to 125 cm3, 11 kW and 0.1 kW/kg; tricycles up to 15 kW; small farm machines; and all AM vehicles. It never turns into A2 or A by itself.
explain.trap: 'solo se lo stesso è maggiorenne' (only if the passenger is an adult) is an invented condition.

sceneParams.caption: Passenger: depends on the vehicle, not age

q24498.reviewNote: Passenger rules for under-18 A1 riders: explained via the registration document (as in q24503); please verify against art. 170 CdS.

q24499.en: After the first two years, the A1 licence automatically becomes an A2 licence and, after two more years, an A licence that allows any motorbike.

explain.short: No licence changes category by itself. To move from A1 to A2, or from A2 to A, you must pass a new driving test.
explain.rule: A1 licence: from 16 years. Motorbikes up to 125 cm3, 11 kW and 0.1 kW/kg; tricycles up to 15 kW; small farm machines; and all AM vehicles. It never turns into A2 or A by itself.
explain.trap: 'automaticamente' (automatically) makes it wrong: each step needs a new test.

sceneParams.caption: A1 never turns into A2 or A by itself
lines: A1 to A2: new test needed
A2 to A: new test needed

q24500.en: With an A2 licence you may drive motorbikes (with or without sidecar) with power up to 35 kW and power/weight ratio not over 0.2 kW/kg, as long as they are not derived from a version of the same model with more than double the maximum power.

explain.short: These are the exact A2 limits: 35 kW, 0.2 kW/kg, and the bike must not be a reduced version of one with more than double the power.
explain.rule: A2 licence: from 18 years. Motorbikes up to 35 kW and 0.2 kW/kg (not derived from a model with more than double the power), plus all A1 and AM vehicles. After 2 years with A2 you can get A at 20.
explain.trap: 'oltre il doppio' (more than double) and 35 kW are the correct numbers.

sceneParams.caption: A2: 35 kW, 0.2 kW/kg, not from double power
lines: Not from a model with double power

q24501.en: The A2 licence also allows you to drive the vehicles that can be driven with the A1 and AM licences.

explain.short: A2 includes the lower motorbike licences: all A1 and AM vehicles.
explain.rule: A2 licence: from 18 years. Motorbikes up to 35 kW and 0.2 kW/kg (not derived from a model with more than double the power), plus all A1 and AM vehicles. After 2 years with A2 you can get A at 20.
explain.trap: 'anche' (also): A2 covers its own motorbikes plus A1 and AM vehicles.

sceneParams.caption: A2 includes A1 and AM vehicles
lines: Also all A1 and AM vehicles

q24502.en: The A2 licence can be obtained by anyone who is at least 18 years old.

explain.short: The minimum age for A2 is 18.
explain.rule: A2 licence: from 18 years. Motorbikes up to 35 kW and 0.2 kW/kg (not derived from a model with more than double the power), plus all A1 and AM vehicles. After 2 years with A2 you can get A at 20.
explain.trap: 18 is the correct number for A2.

sceneParams.caption: A2: from 18 years

q24503.en: The A2 licence allows the holder to carry a passenger only if the passenger seat is stated in the vehicle's registration document.

explain.short: You may carry a passenger only on a motorbike approved for two people, as written in the registration document.
explain.rule: A2 licence: from 18 years. Motorbikes up to 35 kW and 0.2 kW/kg (not derived from a model with more than double the power), plus all A1 and AM vehicles. After 2 years with A2 you can get A at 20.
explain.trap: 'solo se ... previsto sulla carta di circolazione': the registration document decides.

sceneParams.caption: Passenger only if the registration allows it
lines: Yes: you may carry a passenger

q24504.en: Someone who has held the A2 licence for at least two years can get the A licence, valid for all motorbikes, even if under 24.

explain.short: This is gradual access: after 2 years of A2 you can take A at 20. You do not have to wait until 24.
explain.rule: A2 licence: from 18 years. Motorbikes up to 35 kW and 0.2 kW/kg (not derived from a model with more than double the power), plus all A1 and AM vehicles. After 2 years with A2 you can get A at 20.
explain.trap: 'anche se ha meno di 24 anni' (even if under 24) is right: 24 is only for direct access.

sceneParams.caption: 2 years of A2: A licence before 24

q24505.en: The holder of an A2 licence may also drive farm machines within the size and mass limits of motorbike-class vehicles (motoveicoli).

explain.short: A2 includes A1, and A1 allows small farm machines within motoveicoli limits.
explain.rule: A2 licence: from 18 years. Motorbikes up to 35 kW and 0.2 kW/kg (not derived from a model with more than double the power), plus all A1 and AM vehicles. After 2 years with A2 you can get A at 20.
explain.trap: 'anche' (also): A2 inherits the farm machines allowed by A1.

sceneParams.caption: A2: small farm machines allowed

keywords.it: limiti di sagoma e di massa

q24506.en: The A2 licence can be obtained by anyone who is at least 20 years old.

explain.short: The minimum age for A2 is 18, not 20. Age 20 is when you can move from A2 to A.
explain.rule: A2 licence: from 18 years. Motorbikes up to 35 kW and 0.2 kW/kg (not derived from a model with more than double the power), plus all A1 and AM vehicles. After 2 years with A2 you can get A at 20.
explain.trap: The number is wrong: 20 is the age for gradual access to A, not for A2.

sceneParams.caption: A2: from 18, not 20

q24507.en: With an A2 licence you may drive motorbikes (with or without sidecar) with power up to 25 kW and power/weight ratio not over 0.2 kW/kg, as long as they are not derived from a version with more than triple the maximum power.

explain.short: Two numbers are wrong: the A2 limit is 35 kW, and the bike must not come from a version with more than DOUBLE the power.
explain.rule: A2 licence: from 18 years. Motorbikes up to 35 kW and 0.2 kW/kg (not derived from a model with more than double the power), plus all A1 and AM vehicles. After 2 years with A2 you can get A at 20.
explain.trap: '25 kW' and 'triplo' (triple) are wrong; the right values are 35 kW and 'doppio' (double).

sceneParams.caption: A2: 35 kW and double, not 25 kW and triple
lines: Not from DOUBLE power, not triple

q24508.en: Someone who has held the A2 licence for at least two years can get the A licence, valid for all motorbikes, only if they already hold the AM licence and are over 24.

explain.short: After 2 years of A2 you can get A at 20. You do not need AM and you do not need to be over 24.
explain.rule: A2 licence: from 18 years. Motorbikes up to 35 kW and 0.2 kW/kg (not derived from a model with more than double the power), plus all A1 and AM vehicles. After 2 years with A2 you can get A at 20.
explain.trap: 'solo se ... AM ed ha più di 24 anni' adds false conditions.

sceneParams.caption: 2 years of A2: no AM, no age 24 needed

q24509.en: The holder of an A2 licence may not drive motorbikes over 150 cm3 and over 25 kW.

explain.short: A2 has no engine-size limit. Its limit is power: up to 35 kW and 0.2 kW/kg. So a 25 kW bike over 150 cm3 is fine.
explain.rule: A2 licence: from 18 years. Motorbikes up to 35 kW and 0.2 kW/kg (not derived from a model with more than double the power), plus all A1 and AM vehicles. After 2 years with A2 you can get A at 20.
explain.trap: '150 cm3' and '25 kW' are invented limits: A2 counts power (35 kW), not engine size.

sceneParams.caption: A2: no cm3 limit, power up to 35 kW

q24510.en: The A2 licence can be obtained only if you already hold the A1 licence.

explain.short: You can take A2 directly at 18. A1 is not required first.
explain.rule: A2 licence: from 18 years. Motorbikes up to 35 kW and 0.2 kW/kg (not derived from a model with more than double the power), plus all A1 and AM vehicles. After 2 years with A2 you can get A at 20.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) makes it wrong: A1 is not a required step.

sceneParams.caption: A2 does not require A1 first

q24511.en: The A2 licence allows you to drive only mopeds and light quadricycles.

explain.short: A2 is a motorbike licence: motorbikes up to 35 kW, plus all A1 and AM vehicles. Mopeds and light quadricycles are only part of it.
explain.rule: A2 licence: from 18 years. Motorbikes up to 35 kW and 0.2 kW/kg (not derived from a model with more than double the power), plus all A1 and AM vehicles. After 2 years with A2 you can get A at 20.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) makes it wrong: mopeds and light quadricycles are the AM part.

sceneParams.caption: A2: motorbikes too, not only mopeds
lines: Motorbikes up to 35 kW: yes too

q24512.en: The A2 licence does not allow you to drive any kind of motor tricycle.

explain.short: A2 includes A1, and A1 allows tricycles up to 15 kW. So some tricycles are allowed with A2.
explain.rule: A2 licence: from 18 years. Motorbikes up to 35 kW and 0.2 kW/kg (not derived from a model with more than double the power), plus all A1 and AM vehicles. After 2 years with A2 you can get A at 20.
explain.trap: 'alcun tipo' (any kind) is the trap: tricycles up to 15 kW are allowed.

sceneParams.caption: A2: tricycles up to 15 kW allowed

q24513.en: With an A licence you may drive all motorbikes (with or without sidecar).

explain.short: The A licence has no power or size limit for motorbikes: all of them are allowed.
explain.rule: A licence: all motorbikes, plus A2, A1 and AM vehicles. Tricycles over 15 kW only from 21 years. You get it at 20 after 2 years of A2 (gradual access) or at 24 directly. It is valid in all the EU.
explain.trap: 'tutti' (all) is right here: A is the full motorbike licence.

sceneParams.caption: A licence: all motorbikes

q24514.en: With an A licence you may drive all motor tricycles, but only if the driver is at least 21.

explain.short: Tricycles over 15 kW need the driver to be at least 21. So ALL tricycles are allowed only from 21.
explain.rule: A licence: all motorbikes, plus A2, A1 and AM vehicles. Tricycles over 15 kW only from 21 years. You get it at 20 after 2 years of A2 (gradual access) or at 24 directly. It is valid in all the EU.
explain.trap: 'tutti ... ma solo se ... almeno 21 anni': the age 21 is needed for the powerful ones, so for all of them.

sceneParams.caption: All tricycles with A: from 21
lines: Tricycle up to 15 kW: also A1/A2

q24514.reviewNote: Official TRUE, but tricycles up to 15 kW are also A1/A2 vehicles; explained as: age 21 needed for the powerful ones, so for ALL.

q24515.en: The A licence allows you to drive motorbikes over 50 cm3 even if they reach a speed over 45 km/h.

explain.short: Over 50 cm3 and over 45 km/h means a motorbike, not a moped. The A licence covers all motorbikes.
explain.rule: A licence: all motorbikes, plus A2, A1 and AM vehicles. Tricycles over 15 kW only from 21 years. You get it at 20 after 2 years of A2 (gradual access) or at 24 directly. It is valid in all the EU.
explain.trap: 'anche se' (even if) is right: the A licence has no speed limit for motorbikes.

sceneParams.caption: A licence: big and fast motorbikes too
lines: It is a motorbike: A licence OK

q24516.en: The A licence can be obtained by direct access, by someone who has not held an A2 licence for at least 2 years, only if they are 24 or older.

explain.short: Without 2 years of A2, you take A directly, and the minimum age is 24.
explain.rule: A licence: all motorbikes, plus A2, A1 and AM vehicles. Tricycles over 15 kW only from 21 years. You get it at 20 after 2 years of A2 (gradual access) or at 24 directly. It is valid in all the EU.
explain.trap: 'accesso diretto' (direct access) goes with 24 years; 'accesso graduale' with 20.

sceneParams.caption: Direct access to A: age 24

q24517.en: The A licence can be obtained at 20, by gradual access, by someone who has held an A2 licence for at least 2 years.

explain.short: Gradual access: hold A2 for 2 years, then you can get A at 20.
explain.rule: A licence: all motorbikes, plus A2, A1 and AM vehicles. Tricycles over 15 kW only from 21 years. You get it at 20 after 2 years of A2 (gradual access) or at 24 directly. It is valid in all the EU.
explain.trap: 'accesso graduale' (gradual access) goes with 20 years and 2 years of A2.

sceneParams.caption: Gradual access to A: age 20 after 2 years A2

q24518.en: The A licence also allows you to drive the vehicles that can be driven with the A1, A2 and AM licences.

explain.short: A is the top motorbike licence and includes all the lower ones: A2, A1 and AM.
explain.rule: A licence: all motorbikes, plus A2, A1 and AM vehicles. Tricycles over 15 kW only from 21 years. You get it at 20 after 2 years of A2 (gradual access) or at 24 directly. It is valid in all the EU.
explain.trap: 'anche' (also): A covers its own vehicles plus all the lower categories.

sceneParams.caption: A includes A2, A1 and AM
lines: Also all A2, A1 and AM vehicles

q24519.en: With an A licence you may also drive tricycles with power over 15 kW, but only if the driver is at least 21.

explain.short: Powerful tricycles (over 15 kW) are allowed with the A licence from age 21.
explain.rule: A licence: all motorbikes, plus A2, A1 and AM vehicles. Tricycles over 15 kW only from 21 years. You get it at 20 after 2 years of A2 (gradual access) or at 24 directly. It is valid in all the EU.
explain.trap: 'ma solo se ... almeno 21 anni' (only if at least 21) is the correct condition.

sceneParams.caption: Tricycle over 15 kW: A and age 21

q24520.en: With an A licence you may drive motorbikes (with or without sidecar) of any engine size, as long as their power is under 35 kW for the first 2 years after getting it.

explain.short: The A licence has no power limit, not even in the first 2 years. The 35 kW limit belongs to the A2 licence.
explain.rule: A licence: all motorbikes, plus A2, A1 and AM vehicles. Tricycles over 15 kW only from 21 years. You get it at 20 after 2 years of A2 (gradual access) or at 24 directly. It is valid in all the EU.
explain.trap: 'per i primi 2 anni' (for the first 2 years) is invented: it mixes up A with A2.

sceneParams.caption: A licence: no 35 kW limit at the start
lines: A licence: any power from day one

q24521.en: With an A licence you may drive non-light quadricycles, whatever the driver's age.

explain.short: Non-light quadricycles are not A licence vehicles. They need the B1 or B licence.
explain.rule: A licence: all motorbikes, plus A2, A1 and AM vehicles. Tricycles over 15 kW only from 21 years. You get it at 20 after 2 years of A2 (gradual access) or at 24 directly. It is valid in all the EU.
explain.trap: 'quadricicli non leggeri' are four-wheel vehicles: they are not motorbikes.

sceneParams.caption: Non-light quadricycles: B1 or B, not A
lines: Not with A: B1 or B

q24522.en: The A licence can be obtained by gradual access at 18, by someone who has held an A1 licence for at least 2 years.

explain.short: Gradual access to A comes after 2 years of A2, and at age 20. A1 does not lead directly to A.
explain.rule: A licence: all motorbikes, plus A2, A1 and AM vehicles. Tricycles over 15 kW only from 21 years. You get it at 20 after 2 years of A2 (gradual access) or at 24 directly. It is valid in all the EU.
explain.trap: 'A1' and '18 anni' are wrong: gradual access needs A2 and age 20.

sceneParams.caption: Gradual access: from A2 at 20, not A1 at 18

q24523.en: With an A licence you may also drive tricycles with power over 15 kW, whatever the driver's age.

explain.short: Tricycles over 15 kW are allowed with A only from age 21. Age matters.
explain.rule: A licence: all motorbikes, plus A2, A1 and AM vehicles. Tricycles over 15 kW only from 21 years. You get it at 20 after 2 years of A2 (gradual access) or at 24 directly. It is valid in all the EU.
explain.trap: 'qualunque sia l'età' (whatever the age) is wrong: 21 years are needed.

sceneParams.caption: Tricycle over 15 kW: only from 21

q24524.en: The A licence can be obtained by direct access also by someone who has not held an A2 licence for at least 2 years, as long as they are 21.

explain.short: Direct access to the A licence needs age 24, not 21.
explain.rule: A licence: all motorbikes, plus A2, A1 and AM vehicles. Tricycles over 15 kW only from 21 years. You get it at 20 after 2 years of A2 (gradual access) or at 24 directly. It is valid in all the EU.
explain.trap: '21 anni' is the trap: 21 is for tricycles over 15 kW; direct access is 24.

sceneParams.caption: Direct access to A: 24, not 21

q24525.en: The A licence obtained by direct access at 24 or older allows you to drive all motorbikes, but only in Italy; to drive abroad another exam is needed.

explain.short: An Italian licence is an EU licence: it is valid in all EU countries, with no extra exam.
explain.rule: A licence: all motorbikes, plus A2, A1 and AM vehicles. Tricycles over 15 kW only from 21 years. You get it at 20 after 2 years of A2 (gradual access) or at 24 directly. It is valid in all the EU.
explain.trap: 'solo in Italia' (only in Italy) is wrong: the licence is valid in the whole EU.

sceneParams.caption: A licence valid in all the EU

q24526.en: To get the A licence you must in every case be at least 24 years old.

explain.short: Not in every case: with 2 years of A2 you can get A at 20. 24 is only for direct access.
explain.rule: A licence: all motorbikes, plus A2, A1 and AM vehicles. Tricycles over 15 kW only from 21 years. You get it at 20 after 2 years of A2 (gradual access) or at 24 directly. It is valid in all the EU.
explain.trap: 'in ogni caso' (in every case) is the trap: gradual access allows age 20.

sceneParams.caption: 24 only for direct access; 20 with A2

q24527.en: The B1 licence can be obtained at 16 years of age.

explain.short: The minimum age for B1 is 16.
explain.rule: B1 licence: from 16 years, only for non-light quadricycles (also the handlebar 'Quad'). No motorbikes, no tricycles, no cars, no A1 vehicles.
explain.trap: 16 is the correct number for B1.

sceneParams.caption: B1: from 16 years

q24530.en: The B1 licence allows you to drive some types of non-light quadricycles.

explain.short: B1 is the licence for non-light quadricycles (heavier four-wheel vehicles, bigger than a minicar).
explain.rule: B1 licence: from 16 years, only for non-light quadricycles (also the handlebar 'Quad'). No motorbikes, no tricycles, no cars, no A1 vehicles.
explain.trap: 'alcuni tipi' (some types) is careful wording, and correct.

sceneParams.caption: B1: non-light quadricycles

q24531.en: The B1 licence allows you to drive non-light quadricycles with handlebars (Quad).

explain.short: A 'Quad' with handlebars is a non-light quadricycle, so B1 is the right licence.
explain.rule: B1 licence: from 16 years, only for non-light quadricycles (also the handlebar 'Quad'). No motorbikes, no tricycles, no cars, no A1 vehicles.
explain.trap: 'manubrio' (handlebars) does not make it a motorbike: it still has four wheels.

sceneParams.caption: B1: Quad with handlebars

q24532.en: The B1 licence allows you to drive motorbikes (with or without sidecar) up to 125 cm3, power not over 11 kW and power/weight ratio not over 0.1 kW/kg.

explain.short: Those are the A1 motorbike limits. B1 is only for quadricycles, not motorbikes.
explain.rule: B1 licence: from 16 years, only for non-light quadricycles (also the handlebar 'Quad'). No motorbikes, no tricycles, no cars, no A1 vehicles.
explain.trap: The numbers are right, but for A1: 'B1' does not allow motorbikes.

sceneParams.caption: These motorbikes need A1, not B1

q24533.en: With a B1 licence you may drive all motor tricycles, but only if the driver is already 18.

explain.short: B1 does not cover tricycles. Tricycles go with motorbike licences (A1, A2, A) or B.
explain.rule: B1 licence: from 16 years, only for non-light quadricycles (also the handlebar 'Quad'). No motorbikes, no tricycles, no cars, no A1 vehicles.
explain.trap: 'tutti i tricicli' (all tricycles) is wrong: B1 is only for quadricycles.

sceneParams.caption: Tricycles: not with B1

q24534.en: The B1 licence allows you to drive single-seat cars, or cars with at most three seats including the driver, as long as you travel with no passengers.

explain.short: Cars (autovetture) need the B licence. B1 is only for non-light quadricycles.
explain.rule: B1 licence: from 16 years, only for non-light quadricycles (also the handlebar 'Quad'). No motorbikes, no tricycles, no cars, no A1 vehicles.
explain.trap: 'autovetture' (cars) are not quadricycles: the passenger condition is a distraction.

sceneParams.caption: Cars need B, not B1

q24535.en: The B1 licence also allows you to drive the vehicles that can be driven with the A1 licence.

explain.short: B1 does not include A1. A1 motorbikes need the A1 (or A2, A) licence.
explain.rule: B1 licence: from 16 years, only for non-light quadricycles (also the handlebar 'Quad'). No motorbikes, no tricycles, no cars, no A1 vehicles.
explain.trap: 'anche' (also) is the trap: B1 is a separate category, it does not include A1.

sceneParams.caption: B1 does not include A1

q24536.en: A B1 licence holder who wants to get a B licence will only have to take an extra theory exam.

explain.short: Getting B is not just an extra theory exam: you must also pass the driving test for B.
explain.rule: B1 licence: from 16 years, only for non-light quadricycles (also the handlebar 'Quad'). No motorbikes, no tricycles, no cars, no A1 vehicles.
explain.trap: 'solo un esame teorico integrativo' (only an extra theory exam) is the trap: a driving test is needed too.

sceneParams.caption: From B1 to B: driving test needed too

q24536.reviewNote: Explanation says a driving test is also needed to go from B1 to B; exact exam requirement not certain.
